$comment: Decisions about single named items in the coverage queue, read by tools/coverage.mjs. A skip leaves `--queue` for good and says why. A note stays in the queue and hands its text to whoever writes the card, as `reviewNote`. Matching is exact and case-insensitive on the queue name, or on the sanskrit name for asanas, never fuzzy. Started 2026-09-12, when 19 of the top 25 queue items were names earlier passes had already decided against and were re-reading every twelve hours. Every reason is written here in our own words: the free-exercise-db reference is vendored as names only, on purpose (see the licensing note at the top of coverage.mjs), and nothing in this file copies its text.

entries.name: Astavakrasana
entries.reason: Eight-angle pose is an advanced arm balance with the whole body held off bent arms. Described even slightly wrong, the hand or leg placement is a real fall or joint-load risk.

entries.name: Kaundinyasana
entries.reason: An advanced arm balance with the legs extended off the arms, carrying the same fall and wrist-load risk as Astavakrasana if the placement is described even slightly wrong.

entries.name: Durvasasana
entries.reason: A standing pose with one leg taken behind the head: an advanced bind with real hip, knee and lower-back strain risk for anyone learning it from a card.

entries.name: Gorakshasana
entries.reason: Two materially different techniques circulate under this name (soles together sitting on the heels, versus the classical ankle lock) and the reference does not say which one it means.

entries.name: Matsyendrasana
entries.reason: Full lord of the fishes forces one foot into half-lotus against the opposite hip, a well-documented way to injure a knee. The deck already carries the safer half version as yoga-seated-spinal-twist.

entries.name: Marichyasana
entries.reason: Names a family of four poses (A to D) that differ materially, some adding a bind with an arm wrapped behind the back, and the reference does not say which. A wrong bind description is a real strain risk.
entries.by: 2026-09-09 morning Bellows pass; confirmed in review 2026-09-12

entries.name: Adductor/Groin
entries.reason: The movement under this name is a partner-resisted groin stretch: someone else holds your legs and pushes them apart. FitFlexr is used alone. Earlier passes skipped it as an unclear name; needing a second person is the real reason.

entries.name: Band Hip Adductions
entries.reason: The reference contradicts itself: the name says adduction (leg drawn in toward the body) while the movement lifts the leg out to the side, which is abduction. The schema also has no hip-adduction pattern, so this needs a schema decision before it can be a card.

entries.name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
entries.reason: The same skater-style bound as the shipped Lateral Bound, travelling diagonally forward instead of straight sideways. Not different enough to earn its own card.

entries.name: Bench Jump
entries.reason: Clearing a full-height bench in one jump means landing from above it, the landing the shipped Box Jump Over card deliberately avoids by stepping down to protect knees and Achilles. A 2026-09-11 card under this name described fast sideways hops over a bench instead, and was dropped in review.

entries.name: Barbell Curls Lying Against An Incline
entries.reason: A curl lying face-down on an incline bench with a straight bar, which is a barbell spider curl. Same target and audience as the shipped Spider Dumbbell Curl and awkward with a straight bar; a pass reached the same conclusion about a barbell spider curl on 2026-09-12.

entries.name: Alternating Deltoid Raise
entries.reason: Not ambiguous. With a dumbbell in each hand the reps alternate: one front raise to shoulder height, then one side raise to shoulder height, and repeat. Earlier passes skipped it believing the name did not say which raise; it is both, in turn.

entries.name: Anti-Gravity Press
entries.reason: A light shoulder drill, not an overhead press. Lying face-down on an incline bench, the bar starts close to your chest and is pressed straight out in front of your head, arms travelling parallel to the floor, then brought back in.

entries.name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
entries.reason: Lying back on an incline bench with the bar held straight up at arm's length, raise it a few inches using only your shoulder blades, arms staying straight, then lower. A serratus drill; it must not be written as a press.

entries.name: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row
entries.reason: A one-arm landmine row: one end of a barbell anchored in a corner or landmine, plates on the other end, rowed one-handed while the other hand rests on your knee. The two-handed version is the shipped T-Bar Row. If the card gets a different title, give it this name as an alias or coverage keeps queueing it.

entries.name: Barbell Step Ups
entries.reason: Not a duplicate. Step-ups already ship as separate box, dumbbell and kettlebell cards; this is the version with a barbell across the upper back, equipment barbell and box. A 2026-09-12 pass judged it too close to Box Step-Up.

entries.name: Barbell Shoulder Press
entries.reason: Not a duplicate of the shipped Barbell Overhead Press, which is standing. The movement under this name is seated on a bench with back support, equipment barbell and bench, the way dumbbell presses already ship as separate seated and standing cards. Title it Seated Barbell Shoulder Press and keep this name as an alias.

entries.name: Bent Press
entries.reason: An expert-level kettlebell lift whose whole point is that the arm barely moves and the body presses itself out from under the bell via a sideways hip/lat hinge -- the opposite of a normal press. A description that reads as 'press overhead while leaning to the side' would teach the wrong pattern under a loaded, twisted spine, and that residual uncertainty about the exact hip/lat sequencing is enough on its own to skip a spinal-loading lift.

entries.name: Bodyweight Flyes
entries.reason: The reference tags this with e-z curl bar equipment, but a flye is defined by each arm independently arcing outward -- both hands fixed to one bar cannot do that motion, so the name and the equipment contradict each other. Free-exercise-db elsewhere uses this name for a TRX/strap flye, which is a different, plausible movement; without knowing which one this record means, writing either is a guess.

entries.name: Butt Lift (Bridge)
entries.reason: The bodyweight bridge under this name is the shipped Glute Bridge: lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, drive the hips up. No distinguishing detail in the reference separates it from the shipped card.

entries.name: Butterfly
entries.reason: The standard alternate name for the machine chest fly, already shipped as Pec Deck Fly (equipment: machine, same seated-arms-wide-squeeze-together movement).

entries.name: Butt-Ups
entries.reason: Not confident of the exact setup from the name alone -- this could be a kneeling hip-thrust ab drill or something closer to the shipped Glute Bridge/Reverse Crunch family, and the reference gives no instructions to check against. A wrong ab card is worse than a missing one.

entries.name: Cable Incline Pushdown
entries.reason: The reference tags this as a lats exercise, but 'pushdown' as a name is otherwise only used here for triceps cable work. Not confident enough of the incline-bench setup that turns a pushdown into a lat movement to write it without guessing.

entries.name: Cable Iron Cross
entries.reason: A wide-arm cable chest movement pulled in toward center is already covered by the shipped Cable Chest Fly and High/Low Cable Crossover. Not confident the 'iron cross' starting position (arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, rather than a slight bend) is different enough to earn its own card rather than guessing at a distinction that isn't real.

entries.name: Cable Judo Flip
entries.reason: A diagonal rotational cable pull for the obliques reads as the same movement as the shipped Cable Woodchopper. Not confident there's a real distinguishing detail behind the name rather than a second title for the same chop.

entries.name: Cable Lying Triceps Extension
entries.reason: Lying on a bench facing away from a low pulley, gripping a rope or bar behind the head and extending overhead, reads as the same setup and movement as the just-shipped Cable Incline Triceps Extension — only the bench angle differs, which is not a distinct exercise.

entries.name: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows
entries.reason: A rope pulled toward the face/upper chest with elbows flared and high, targeting the rear delts and upper back, is the shipped Cable Face Pull. Not confident there's a real distinguishing pull path (to the chest with elbows back, rather than to the face with elbows up) behind the name rather than a second title for the same pull.

entries.name: Calf Stretch Hands Against Wall
entries.reason: Word-for-word the shipped Standing Calf Stretch (tf-standing-calf-stretch): 'both hands on it', one foot back, heel pressed into the floor, leg straight. No distinguishing detail in the reference separates it from the shipped card.

entries.name: Calf-Machine Shoulder Shrug
entries.reason: Uses a standing calf-raise machine's shoulder pads to shrug instead of raise the heels. Standing calf machines are not one standardized geometry (platform height, pad angle, knee-lock position vary by brand), and F10's lesson is exactly this: a confidently wrong setup description on unfamiliar equipment is worse than no card. Cable Shrug and the existing Dumbbell/Barbell Shrug already cover the movement pattern.

entries.name: Cat Stretch
entries.reason: The reference gives name and equipment only (bodyweight, stretching, lower back). The shipped Cat-Cow (yoga-cat-cow) is the same hands-and-knees spine-rounding movement; nothing in the reference distinguishes a standalone 'Cat Stretch' from the cat half of that pose.

entries.name: Chair Squat
entries.reason: Tagged equipment 'machine' in the reference, but the name describes a bodyweight sit-to-a-chair squat with no machine involved. That mismatch between name and equipment is the exact class of error F10 warns about — writing a setup for whichever reading is wrong would ship a confidently incorrect card.

entries.name: Chest Push (multiple response)
entries.reason: A medicine-ball plyometric combine drill. The reference gives no instructions, and 'multiple response' vs 'single response' vs '3 point stance' vs 'run release' are four variants of the same throw distinguished only by stance and rep scheme — details easy to conflate from the name alone, and this app has no rebounder/wall-toss equipment concept to anchor which setup is meant.

entries.name: Chest Push (single response)
entries.reason: Same medicine-ball chest-push family as 'Chest Push (multiple response)' — see that entry. Not confident which setup detail (wall vs partner, stance) separates it from the other three variants.

entries.name: Chest Push from 3 point stance
entries.reason: Same medicine-ball chest-push family as 'Chest Push (multiple response)' — see that entry. Not confident which setup detail separates it from the other three variants.

entries.name: Chest Push with Run Release
entries.reason: Same medicine-ball chest-push family as 'Chest Push (multiple response)' — see that entry. Not confident which setup detail separates it from the other three variants.

entries.name: Clean
entries.reason: Barbell, floor-to-shoulders, the shipped Barbell Clean (barbell-clean-conditioning) already is this movement under a fuller name.

entries.name: Clean from Blocks
entries.reason: A full clean, catch and all, starting with the bar on elevated blocks instead of the floor. The catch is the hardest part of a clean to describe correctly (Clean and Jerk's own catch needed a correction in the 2026-09-14 review), and 'blocks' commonly means either below-knee or above-knee height with no way to tell which this name intends. Not confident enough to write either detail.

entries.name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Curl with Band
entries.reason: A close-grip EZ-bar curl with a resistance band looped around the bar ends and anchored underfoot for accommodating resistance. Not confident describing the band anchor and stance precisely from the name alone — the base movement shipped this pass as Close-Grip EZ-Bar Curl.

entries.name: Close-Grip Front Lat Pulldown
entries.reason: Same movement as the shipped Close-Grip Cable Lat Pulldown (close-grip-cable-lat-pulldown) — 'front' just means pulled to the chest rather than behind the neck, which that card already describes.

entries.name: Close-Grip Standing Barbell Curl
entries.reason: Same movement as the shipped Close-Grip Barbell Curl (close-grip-barbell-curl), which is already standing — 'standing' names nothing that card doesn't already do.

entries.name: Crunch - Legs On Exercise Ball
entries.reason: Needs a stability/exercise ball, which has no equipment id in EQUIPMENT — tagging it bodyweight would be the same furniture-mislabeling error the 2026-09-13 review fixed on bench/box cards. Adding a new equipment id is a structural decision beyond a card batch.

entries.name: Crunches
entries.reason: Plain floor crunch, hands by the head — the shipped Crunch (crunch) under a plural title. No distinguishing detail in the reference.

entries.name: Dancer's Stretch
entries.reason: The reference gives name and one muscle (lower back) only. Standing, grabbing the ankle behind you and hinging forward is the same starting shape as the shipped King Dancer Pose (Natarajasana) — not confident whether this names a simpler stretch without the backbend/overhead reach or is the same pose under its dance-studio name, and writing either is a guess.

entries.name: Decline Close-Grip Bench To Skull Crusher
entries.reason: The name implies a hybrid rep that transitions from a close-grip bench press into a skull crusher within one movement, on a decline bench. Not confident of the exact transition point or bar path from the name alone, and it overlaps the shipped Barbell Skull Crusher and EZ-Bar/Dumbbell JM Press family closely enough that a wrong guess at the hybrid detail is worse than skipping it.

entries.name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
entries.reason: No kettlebell jerk of any kind is shipped yet to pattern-match against, and the jerk's dip-drive-catch is exactly the technical-catch class of movement OPERATING.md and the Clean-from-Blocks skip both flag as the hardest part to describe correctly. Not confident enough to write the catch timing from the name alone.

entries.name: Double Kettlebell Snatch
entries.reason: Same technical-catch class the Double Kettlebell Jerk skip already flags: the snatch's bell-rolls-to-lockout catch is the hardest part of the single-arm version to get right (the shipped Kettlebell Snatch card calls it 'powerful and technical'), and doing it with two bells simultaneously doubles the chance of a wrong wrist-rotation detail teaching someone to bang their forearms.

entries.name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation
entries.reason: A real forearm-rotation exercise, but not confident of the exact body position from the name alone -- lying on the back with the working forearm resting across the body, lying on the side, or seated with the forearm on a bench are all plausible readings and the reference gives no instructions to check against. A wrong setup on a small-ROM rotational movement is an easy way to teach the wrong joint action.

entries.name: Dumbbell Lying Supination
entries.reason: Same family and same uncertainty as Dumbbell Lying Pronation -- see that entry.

entries.name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
entries.reason: Duplicate of the already-shipped prone-dumbbell-curl: 'lie face-down on a flat bench raised enough for your arms to hang' is the same body position and the same anti-swing mechanism an incline bench gives this move. Writing a second card for it would ship two entries for one exercise.

entries.name: Dumbbell Seated Box Jump
entries.reason: The name alone doesn't say whether the seated start is on the ground, a low box or the target box, and holding dumbbells through a plyometric landing is a real grip-and-balance risk that a wrongly-guessed setup would only make worse.

entries.name: Dynamic Back Stretch
entries.reason: "Back" covers upper (thoracic rotation/extension) and lower back movement patterns that are not interchangeable, and the name alone does not say which one this is meant to be.

entries.name: Elbows Back
entries.reason: No stable, recognizable movement attaches to this name -- it reads like a cue fragment from a longer routine rather than a named exercise, and guessing a full setup around it risks inventing a stretch that isn't the one meant.
